content: The Gospel text (the story), the poems of Picander (the response of one person), and the chorales (the response of the congregation)
parameters: Sections: 43 Gospel recitatives, 18 choruses of the crowd, 15 arias, 11 recitatives with instruments, 12 plain chorales, 4 large choruses

content: Part 1 has movements 1 to 29, part 2 has movements 30 to 68. A sermon was between the parts
parameters: 29 + 39 movements

content: A scene starts with Gospel text and ends on an aria, a chorale, or a chorus. The two parts start with a chorus or an aria
parameters: 16 scenes; the booklet of one recording gives 9 larger scenes

content: Two choirs in dialogue ("Sehet!" - "Wen?"), and above them the chorale "O Lamm Gottes, unschuldig" as a third layer
parameters: E minor, 12/8. The chorale is in G major. In the first version an instrument played the chorale

content: The bass voice starts on E and goes up by step in the rhythm quarter, eighth
parameters: e, fis, g, then fis and gis to a: the line of bar 17 in the bass

content: A tenor tells the story in recitative with continuo only. Each syllable has one note
parameters: First phrases of four sections: from E-flat 3 to B-flat 4, in eighth notes and sixteenth notes

content: The words of Jesus have long chords of the strings around them: the "halo"
parameters: Instruments of these sections: 2 violins, viola, continuo

content: Only the last words ("Eli, Eli, lama asabthani?") have no strings
parameters: Instruments of the section: continuo only

content: The words of groups. The two choirs sing in turns, or together, or one choir alone (the disciples are always choir 1)
parameters: Short: 5 to 18 bars in five sections of the incipit data

content: A fugue subject with the shape of a cross. The second time it is one whole tone higher
parameters: 45b: A minor to B major. 50b: B minor to C-sharp major. Subject: A, A, G-sharp, C, B, D-sharp, A, G, F-sharp, G, A, B-flat

content: "Truly, this was the Son of God": the two choirs together, as one voice
parameters: 2 bars in A-flat major

content: The tune "Herzlich tut mich verlangen" comes five times with different words and chords
parameters: Keys: E major, E-flat major, D major, D minor to F major, A minor. The last setting ends on the dominant (measured)

content: The first chorale of the work comes three times. In movement 19 the choir sings it between the lines of the tenor
parameters: Keys: B minor; F minor to G major; B minor

content: The disciples ask "Herr, bin ich's?". The chorale answers: "Ich bin's, ich sollte büßen"
parameters: Chorus in F minor to C minor; chorale in A-flat major

element: Recitative with instruments before an aria
content: A short free movement with one fixed figure in the instruments. The aria follows with the same voice
parameters: Example: movement 5, flutes in thirds above a plucked bass

content: The instrument is an equal partner of the voice
parameters: Erbarme dich: the violin has 2.2 notes for each quarter note, the alto has 0.9 (measured)

content: "Aus Liebe will mein Heiland sterben": flute and two oboes da caccia; no strings and no continuo
parameters: A minor, 3/4. The oboes da caccia have repeated quarter notes, staccato

content: One voice sings; the second choir answers with questions or calls ("Wohin?")
The three movements in 12/8: the opening chorus, "Erbarme dich", and "Mache dich, mein Herze, rein"
parameters: Keys: E minor, B minor, B-flat major

content: The last chorus is a slow dance in 3/4 in da capo form. The last chord of C minor has the note B above it, which goes to C
parameters: C minor; 128 bars with the repeat in the edition

element: Tears and blows in the instruments
content: Flutes play staccato when the alto sings of tears that fall. A dotted rhythm without pause shows the scourging
parameters: Movement 51: a dotted sixteenth and a thirty-second, 16 times in one bar

content: A fast chorus in 3/8 on a bass theme of broken chords. In 63a the continuo has runs of thirty-second notes
parameters: 27b: E minor, 3/8; the theme starts in the bass

content: The work starts in E minor (one sharp) and ends in C minor (three flats). The death scene is in the flat keys
parameters: First key E minor; last key C minor; movement 59: A-flat major; movement 63b: A-flat major

content: Almost all Gospel text is in 4/4. The arias and the large choruses have the other metres
parameters: 12/8: 3 movements. 3/8: 4. 3/4: 5. 6/8: 1. 6/4: a part of movement 11

content: Each aria has its own instruments. Recorders come in one movement only; the viola da gamba in four
parameters: Recorders: 19. Oboes da caccia: 19, 48, 49, 59, 60, 65. Viola da gamba: 34, 35, 56, 57. Solo violin: 39, 42

content: The alto has three arias, two arias with the second choir, three recitatives with instruments, and one duet with the soprano
parameters: Keys of the arias: F-sharp minor, B minor, B minor, G minor, E-flat major

content: The story ends at the tomb. The last words are "Ruhe sanfte, sanfte ruh"
In the first version the first choir had a lute. Later the viola da gamba has its part
